_note: Sofia's research file: what each site is, where the analogy breaks down, how it helps exploration. Draft text; [brackets] = still to research. Coordinates in scores.csv are approximate (not yet checked on a map).

Haughton Crater.why: About 20 km impact crater in a cold polar desert; long-running NASA analog site.
Haughton Crater.breaks: 24-hour sun during the summer field season, so no lasting shadow while crews are there.
Haughton Crater.helps: [to research: what has been tested there]

Atacama (Yungay area).why: One of the driest places on Earth, with very high UV.
Atacama (Yungay area).breaks: Warm and near the tropics: no polar lighting and no long shadows.

Rjukan valley.why: Deep east-west valley; the town gets no direct sun for about six months a year.
Rjukan valley.breaks: Green, wet and inhabited: nothing like bare lunar ground.
Rjukan valley.helps: [to research: the town's sun mirrors as a model for lighting dark craters]

Viganella.why: Alpine village without direct sun from November to February.

Seydisfjordur fjord.why: Narrow fjord with little sun even in summer.

Kali Gandaki gorge (Lete).why: Deep gorge between Dhaulagiri and Annapurna.

Kagbeni (Upper Mustang).why: Dry, high valley in the Himalayan rain shadow (team photos).
